reproduction_target: Benchmarking of genomic (GBS SNP), phenomic (FT-NIR) and metabolomic (untargeted UHPLC-HRMS) prediction models for 29 agronomic traits in the grapevine biparental population 50025 (IJ119 x Divona), with across-population transfer to populations 44910 (n=242) and RIxGW (n=254) and across-year transfer over 2019-2021. The computational reproduction target is: (i) GBS variant calling and marker processing - read alignment to PN40024.v4, SNP discovery/filtering with Stacks (DP>=4, AD>2, MAF>0.005), imputation with Beagle; (ii) omics feature preprocessing - Savitzky-Golay first-derivative transformation of FT-NIR spectra, Compound Discoverer 3.3.3.200 processing of the LC-MS data (ChromAlign retention-time alignment, peak-rating and gap-fill thresholds), SERRF batch-effect correction, CDmean selection of the 150-individual metabolomics reference set; (iii) feature-wise BLUP extraction and broad-sense heritability estimation from a mixed model; (iv) the seven prediction frameworks fitted in R - rrBLUP/GBLUP (rrBLUP), BayesCpi and RKHS (BGLR), LASSO and Elastic Net (glmnet), Random Forest (ranger, 100 trees), plus multi-omics BayesCpi and multi-kernel RKHS; (v) the three validation schemes and the Pearson-r accuracy assessment. The physical work (vineyard/greenhouse trial establishment and maintenance, three years of agronomic phenotyping, DNA extraction and ApeKI GBS library preparation and sequencing, tissue sampling/drying/milling, FT-NIR spectral acquisition on the Bruker TANGO, methanol metabolite extraction, and UHPLC-HRMS acquisition on the Vanquish Flex / Exploris 120) is data generation and is out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full text. WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on both the .source.xml and the .full landing page, so the JATS XML was retrieved with curl using a browser User-Agent into an isolated per-paper directory (/tmp/stage1_10.1101_2025.10.24.684307/paper.xml) and tag-stripped locally; the stripped text was verified to contain the exact title phrase 'metabolomic prediction models in biparental grapevine' and the population identifiers 50025 / 44910 / RIxGW before scoring, so no cross-assessor fetch swap occurred. THE PAPER STATES NO CODE REPOSITORY. Greps over the full stripped text return zero hits for 'Code availability', 'github', 'gitlab', 'zenodo', 'figshare', 'docker', 'renv', 'sessionInfo', 'R version' and 'R Core'; the two 'conda' hits are substrings of 'secondary' and the four 'script' hits are substrings of 'prohibitive'/'description'/'manuscript'. There is therefore no repository landing page and no README to read at stage 1. The only availability statement in the manuscript is: 'Data availability. The raw datasets generated for this study are accessible on the data.gouv public repository at: https://doi.org/10.57745/NDN2LL'. Version pins in prose: exactly ONE - 'Compound Discoverer software 3.3.3.200 (Thermo Scientific)', which is vendor instrument-data-processing software. Every tool in the analysis stack proper is unversioned: the read aligner is not even named ('Reads were aligned to PN40024.v4'), and Stacks, Beagle, R itself, glmnet, rrBLUP, BGLR and ranger are named with no version. PN40024.v4 is a reference-genome version, not a software version, and is scored as a data/resource pin rather than on the version axis. No RNG seed is reported anywhere, although five-fold cross-validation, Random Forest and MCMC-based BGLR fitting are all stochastic.

steps.label: Alignment of GBS reads to the PN40024.v4 grapevine reference genome (Velt et al., 2023) - 'Reads were aligned to PN40024.v4'. The aligner is NOT NAMED anywhere in the manuscript, no version, no parameters, and no supplementary methods reference for it; the reference-genome version (v4) is the only thing pinned.

SNP discovery and initial filtering with Stacks (Catchen et al., 2013) - 'SNP discovery and initial filtering followed Stacks'. Quality thresholds are partially given: 'read depth DP >= 4 and allelic depth AD > 2; monomorphic loci were removed using MAF > 0.005'. NO Stacks version, no ustacks/gstacks/populations module settings, no population map, no -r/-p completeness thresholds.

Imputation of missing genotypes with Beagle - the entire description is 'Missing data were imputed with Beagle (Pook et al., 2020)'. NO version, NO parameters (no ne, nitations/burnin, window/overlap, no reference panel statement), and the citation given is to Pook et al. 2020 rather than to a Beagle release.

Selection of the 150-individual metabolomics reference subset from population 50025 using the CDmean optimization criterion (Rincent et al., 2012) - 'Untargeted metabolomics was performed on 150 individuals from population 50025, selected using the CDmean optimization criterion to maximize representativeness of the reference set'. The target size (150) is given, but no implementation (package/script), no version, no optimization settings (exchange algorithm, iterations, RNG seed), and the resulting individual list is not enumerated in the text.

FT-NIR spectral preprocessing by Savitzky-Golay first derivative - 'spectra were transformed using the Savitzky-Golay first derivative (Savitzky and Golay, 1964), consistent with prior work in grapevine phenomic selection (Brault et al., 2022a)'. The derivative order is stated but the window width, polynomial order, and the R package/function used are not; no version; no statement of whether any scatter correction (SNV/MSC) preceded it.

Untargeted LC-MS feature detection and consolidation with Compound Discoverer software 3.3.3.200 (Thermo Scientific) - the ONLY exact version pin in the manuscript. Steps stated verbatim: '(1) retention-time alignment was performed with ChromAlign (Sadygov et al., 2006); (2) components were retained for further processing if peak rating >= 4 in at least 4 samples; (3) the ions were searched in the entire dataset, with a tolerance of 5 ppm, and with a detection threshold (ratio S/B) applied at 1.5 (fill gap)'. Proprietary closed-source GUI software; the Compound Discoverer workflow template (.cdProcessingWF) is not deposited, so the remaining node settings are unrecoverable.

Batch-effect correction of the metabolomics matrix by QC correction using SERRF (systematic error removal with random forests, 200 trees) (Fan et al., 2019) - 'batch-effect correction was carried out by QC correction using systematic error removal with random forests (SERRF) method (200 trees)'. The tree count is given, but no SERRF version/implementation (R package vs web server vs Compound Discoverer node), no QC-sample design (number/placement of QC injections), and no RNG seed for a random-forest-based correction.

Feature-wise genotypic BLUP extraction and broad-sense heritability estimation for every NIR wavelength and every metabolite in population 50025 - the mixed model (random genotype effect, fixed Sample effect, residual) and the heritability formula H2 = sigma2(Genotype) / (sigma2(Genotype) + sigma2(Residual)/n(Sample)) are written out in full. However the fitting software is NOT NAMED (no lme4/asreml/sommer/breedR statement), no version, no convergence/REML settings, and no filtering rule for features that failed to converge.

Ridge-based linear prediction models rrBLUP and GBLUP fitted with the R package rrBLUP (Endelman, 2011) - 'All analyses were conducted in R using established packages: glmnet, rrBLUP, BGLR, ranger'. NO R version, NO rrBLUP version. The GBLUP kinship/similarity matrix K is described only as 'computed from the omics data' with no construction method stated (VanRaden vs centered-scaled vs Gaussian), and no marker centering/scaling rule is given.

BayesCpi variable-selection model estimated with BGLR (Perez and de los Campos, 2014) - model written out with the pi inclusion probability and polygenic term. NO BGLR version, and none of the MCMC controls that determine the result are reported: no nIter, no burnIn, no thin, no prior hyperparameters (df0/S0/probIn/counts), no chain count, no convergence diagnostic, no RNG seed.

Penalized regression - LASSO (Tibshirani, 1996) and Elastic Net (Zou and Hastie, 2005) - 'Both were implemented with glmnet'. NO glmnet version; the Elastic Net alpha mixing parameter is not stated or described as tuned; the lambda path and the lambda-selection rule (cv.glmnet, lambda.min vs lambda.1se, inner-fold count) are not described; standardization setting not stated.

Random Forest regression (Breiman, 2001) - 'Models were fitted with ranger using 100 trees' (Wright and Ziegler, 2017). The tree count is pinned, but NO ranger version, no mtry, no min.node.size, no splitrule, no sample.fraction, and no RNG seed for a stochastic ensemble applied to high-dimensional (wavelength/metabolite) inputs.

Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) regression (de los Campos et al., 2009) - 'RKHS models were run in BGLR'. NO BGLR version; the kernel matrix K is described only as 'the kernel matrix of pairwise similarities' with no kernel family, no bandwidth/theta value or bandwidth-selection procedure (single kernel vs kernel averaging), and no MCMC settings or seed.

Multi-omics extensions combining two or three of genomic (G), phenomic (P) and metabolomic (M) layers - multi-omics BayesCpi (separate variance component per omics block) and multi-kernel RKHS (K1, K2 similarity matrices, Knoch et al., 2021), both in BGLR. Model equations are given, but NO version, no per-block scaling rule, no kernel bandwidths, no MCMC settings, no seed, and no statement of how individuals present in one omics layer but missing from another (metabolomics covers only 150 of 250 individuals) are handled.

Prediction scenarios and accuracy assessment - three validation schemes stated verbatim: 'Five-fold cross-validation where populations were randomly divided into five folds and prediction accuracy measured as Pearson's r between observed and predicted values; Across-population prediction where models were trained in one biparental population and applied to another; Across-year prediction where models were trained on one year (2019 - 2021) or multi-year BLUPs from 50025 was used to predict another year or mean phenotypes from 44910 and RIxGW'. The fold count and the accuracy metric are pinned, but the number of CV repetitions is not stated, no RNG seed is given for the random fold assignment, no stratification rule is described, and there is no released driver code that orders the scenario grid (7 frameworks x 4 tissue-x-timepoint strategies x 29 traits) or maps it to the reported figures and tables.

headline.static_readiness: 0/15 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 1/15 computational steps (6.7%). Only C6 (Compound Discoverer 3.3.3.200) reaches RI, because it is the single step whose invoked software carries an exact version in Methods prose. The other 14/15 steps cap at NI on the version axis: the read aligner is not named at all (C1), and Stacks, Beagle, R itself, glmnet, rrBLUP, BGLR and ranger are named with no version whatsoever ('All analyses were conducted in R using established packages: glmnet, rrBLUP, BGLR, ranger'). No step reaches X, because the binding limitation is not data access - the raw datasets are deposited in a public repository under https://doi.org/10.57745/NDN2LL, which resolves 200 OK to entrepot.recherche.data.gouv.fr. The binding limitations are (a) a complete absence of released code - there is no Code availability statement, no repository, no script archive, no workflow file and no parameter file anywhere in the manuscript, so the driver that orders 7 statistical frameworks x 4 tissue-x-timepoint strategies x 29 traits x 3 validation schemes does not exist publicly; (b) a complete absence of software versions for the analysis stack; and (c) the absence of any RNG seed despite five-fold random CV, Random Forest ensembles, SERRF random-forest correction, CDmean stochastic optimization and MCMC-based BGLR fitting, which alone prevents byte-identical reproduction even if all code were released. Note that the RI on C6 rests on proprietary closed-source vendor software whose workflow template is not deposited, so its practical reproducibility is weaker than the axis score suggests.
headline.coverage: 15 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full-text Methods prose. No repository landing page or README exists to read, because the paper states no code repository of its own; the JATS XML was the sole source. 7 physical wet-lab / data-generation steps counted in W and not verdicted: (1) establishment and maintenance of the 50025 greenhouse collection (n=250) and vineyard trial (n=209, three plants per genotype, two blocks, one unsprayed and one protected), plus the 44910 (n=242) and RIxGW (n=254) trials; (2) agronomic phenotyping - 29 traits over 2019-2021 for 50025, 23 traits over 2020-2021 for 44910, 14 traits over 2017-2018 for RIxGW, with trait definitions and scoring protocols in supplementary Table S7; (3) leaf DNA extraction and genotyping-by-sequencing with ApeKI digestion (Elshire et al., 2011); (4) 2023 tissue sampling of winter wood and leaves at defined phenophases, oven-drying 3 days at 70 C and milling; (5) FT-NIR spectral acquisition on a TANGO (Bruker) spectrometer over ~800-2500 nm (12,500-4,000 cm-1); (6) metabolite extraction - freeze-drying, TissueLyser II bead milling, 50 uL/mg methanol with chloramphenicol internal standard at 5 mg/L, 10 min sonication, centrifugation 12000 g at 10 C for 10 min, with an additional microwave extraction step and a second sonication-centrifugation cycle for wood; (7) UHPLC-HRMS acquisition on a Vanquish Flex system with an Acquity HSS T3 column (100 x 2.1 mm, 1.8 um, 100 A) at 30 C, acetonitrile/formic acid and water/formic acid gradient at 0.33 mL/min, 1 uL injection, coupled to an Exploris 120 Q-Orbitrap (HESI, +/-3.0 kV, 60,000 fwhm at m/z 200, scan range m/z 85-1200, EASY-IC calibration).

gaps.missing: The paper contains NO Code availability statement, no repository (zero hits for github/gitlab/zenodo/figshare across the full text), no script archive, no workflow file and no supplementary code. The sole availability statement is data-only: 'Data availability. The raw datasets generated for this study are accessible on the data.gouv public repository at: https://doi.org/10.57745/NDN2LL'. Consequently none of the following exist publicly: the GBS calling commands, the Savitzky-Golay preprocessing script, the mixed-model BLUP/heritability script, the seven model-fitting scripts, the multi-omics kernel/block construction code, the cross-validation and cross-population/cross-year driver that orders the full scenario grid, and the figure/table generation code. Everything below is a downstream consequence of this single absence.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the R scripts and command lines for all fifteen steps in a public repository, tag a release matching the manuscript, archive it to Zenodo or Software Heritage, and cite the resulting DOI or commit SHA in a Code availability statement alongside the existing data DOI.

gaps.where: C1 (aligner), C2 Stacks, C3 Beagle, C4 CDmean implementation, C5 Savitzky-Golay implementation, C7 SERRF, C8 mixed-model fitter, C9 rrBLUP, C10/C13/C14 BGLR, C11 glmnet, C12 ranger, and R itself
gaps.missing: Fourteen of fifteen computational steps invoke software with NO version pin. Worse, three steps do not name the software at all: the read aligner in C1 ('Reads were aligned to PN40024.v4'), the Savitzky-Golay implementation in C5, and the mixed-model fitting engine in C8. The R version is never stated and no sessionInfo() output is provided. The only version string in the manuscript is Compound Discoverer 3.3.3.200, which is vendor instrument software rather than part of the analysis stack. Because rrBLUP, BGLR, glmnet and ranger have all changed defaults across releases, and Stacks and Beagle have changed calling/imputation behaviour across major versions, the reported predictive abilities cannot be pinned to a software state.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version of R and of every package (glmnet, rrBLUP, BGLR, ranger, and whatever provides Savitzky-Golay and the mixed-model fit), the exact Stacks and Beagle releases, and name the read aligner with its version and command line. Include sessionInfo() output as supplementary material.

gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind is claimed: no lockfile (renv.lock, conda-lock, pixi), no container image or digest, no environment.yml, no module list. Greps return zero hits for 'docker', 'renv' and 'sessionInfo', and the two 'conda' hits are substrings of the word 'secondary'. Because there is not even a floating package list with versions, there is no closure over the R interpreter, BLAS/LAPACK backend (which affects kernel decompositions in GBLUP/RKHS), or the C/C++ toolchain behind ranger and BGLR. This is why the single version-pinned step (C6) is capped at version=1 rather than 2, and why stage-2 execution could not lift any step above RI without newly constructing an environment capture.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock or conda-lock file, or a container image referenced by digest, pinning R, the four modelling packages, the BLAS backend, Stacks, Beagle and the aligner together with their transitive dependencies.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C7, C9, C10, C11, C12, C13, C14, C15 - stochastic controls and hyperparameters
gaps.missing: NO RNG SEED IS REPORTED ANYWHERE, despite at least five stochastic components: five-fold random fold assignment (C15), Random Forest ensembles (C12), SERRF random-forest batch correction (C7), CDmean subset optimization (C4), and MCMC sampling in every BGLR model (C10, C13, C14). Additional unstated parameters: aligner settings and the entire C1 command (nothing given); Stacks module settings, population map and completeness thresholds beyond DP/AD/MAF (C2); all Beagle parameters (C3); Savitzky-Golay window width and polynomial order and any preceding scatter correction (C5); Elastic Net alpha and the lambda-selection rule/inner-fold structure (C11); ranger mtry, min.node.size, splitrule (C12); BGLR nIter, burnIn, thin, priors, chain count and convergence diagnostics (C10, C13, C14); RKHS kernel family and bandwidth or bandwidth-averaging scheme (C13, C14); per-block scaling and missing-layer handling for the multi-omics models, which matters because metabolomics covers only 150 of the 250 genotypes (C14); and the number of cross-validation repetitions (C15).
gaps.how_to_close: Report the RNG seed(s) and the exact repetition counts, publish the full parameter set for every invocation (Stacks modules, Beagle options, Savitzky-Golay window/order, glmnet alpha and lambda rule, ranger mtry/min.node.size, BGLR nIter/burnIn/thin/priors, RKHS bandwidths), and state the rule used to align individuals across omics layers of unequal coverage.

gaps.where: Run order and figure/table provenance across C1-C15
gaps.missing: There is no run-order documentation and no mapping from computational steps to reported figures and tables. The scenario grid is large - seven statistical frameworks x four tissue-x-timepoint strategies (wood; vineyard leaves at budbreak; vineyard leaves at flowering; greenhouse leaves at flowering) x 29 traits x three validation schemes - but the manuscript does not state the iteration order, which intermediate matrices are cached and reused (feature-wise BLUPs vs raw feature values as model input), or which of the reported figures/supplementary tables each invocation produced. Because no repository exists, there is no README or workflow file carrying this information either.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a driver script or workflow (Snakemake/Nextflow/targets) whose rule graph names each step's inputs and outputs, and add a table mapping every manuscript figure and supplementary table to the invocation that produced it.

gaps.where: Data availability DOI 10.57745/NDN2LL and the inherited phenotype BLUPs
gaps.missing: The deposit is referenced by a single blanket sentence - 'The raw datasets generated for this study are accessible on the data.gouv public repository' - with no file manifest, no per-step mapping, no file-level checksums and no version/draft identifier for the Dataverse dataset. It is therefore not determinable from the paper which of the five distinct data products (GBS reads or VCF, FT-NIR spectra, LC-MS feature matrix, phenotype records, feature-wise BLUPs) are present, at which processing stage, or for which of the three populations; in particular the manuscript gives no sequence-archive accession (no SRA/ENA/BioProject) for the ApeKI GBS reads. Separately, part of the phenotypic input is inherited rather than deposited: 'Previously estimated multi-year BLUPs are available from earlier work and were used where indicated (Chedid, 2023; Chedid et al., 2025, 2023)', which routes a load-bearing input through a PhD thesis (https://theses.hal.science/tel-04146149) and two journal papers rather than through the deposit. Trait definitions and scoring protocols live only in supplementary Table S7, which was not opened at stage 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a file manifest with checksums and a pinned dataset version for the Recherche Data Gouv deposit, map each file to the step that consumes it, deposit the raw GBS reads in SRA/ENA with a BioProject accession, and include the inherited multi-year BLUPs as a file in the deposit rather than by citation.

gaps.missing: The single version-pinned step runs on proprietary, licence-gated vendor software with a GUI workflow. The executed code is not obtainable, and the Compound Discoverer processing workflow template (which fixes dozens of node settings beyond the four thresholds reported - mass tolerances per node, peak detection settings, adduct/isotope grouping rules, compound-annotation database selections) is not deposited. Only four settings are stated: ChromAlign retention-time alignment, peak rating >= 4 in at least 4 samples, 5 ppm ion-search tolerance, and S/B ratio 1.5 for gap filling. An independent group without a Thermo licence cannot execute this step at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the Compound Discoverer processing and consensus workflow templates with the data, publish the resulting feature table (m/z, retention time, intensity per sample) as the reproducible entry point for all downstream steps, and where possible provide an open-source equivalent path (XCMS/MZmine) with its parameters for cross-checking.

gaps.missing: Vineyard and greenhouse trial establishment for three biparental populations; three years of agronomic phenotyping (29/23/14 traits); leaf DNA extraction and ApeKI GBS library preparation and sequencing; 2023 tissue sampling, oven-drying and milling; FT-NIR acquisition on the Bruker TANGO; methanol metabolite extraction with chloramphenicol internal standard; and UHPLC-HRMS acquisition on the Vanquish Flex / Exploris 120. These are physical data-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W (7), not verdicted. A full description of the population, experimental layouts, phenotyping and genotyping is deferred to Chedid (2023), a PhD thesis, rather than given in the manuscript - relevant to wet-lab replication but not to the computational readiness score.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the reproducible computational entry point would be the deposited raw datasets at https://doi.org/10.57745/NDN2LL once a per-file manifest exists.
